content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the properties of transition metals
Compare transition metals with Group 1 metals
Explain why transition metals have variable oxidation states
Give examples of coloured compounds and catalytic properties

are found in the central block of the periodic table (d-block). They include many familiar metals like iron, copper, and gold. They have distinctive properties that make them useful in many applications.
[DIAGRAM: Periodic table with transition metal block (Groups 3-12) highlighted in centre]
Transition metals can form ions with different charges:
Transition metals have electrons in both 4s and 3d orbitals
Different numbers of electrons can be lost
Due to partially filled d orbitals
Electrons absorb certain wavelengths of light
Transition metals and their compounds are excellent catalysts:
Variable oxidation states allow electron transfer
Can form temporary bonds with reactants
Compare the properties of sodium (Group 1) and iron (transition metal).
Iron forms two chlorides: FeCl₂ and FeCl₃. Explain why iron can form two different chlorides.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states
Iron can lose 2 electrons to form Fe²⁺ (in FeCl₂)
Iron can lose 3 electrons to form Fe³⁺ (in FeCl₃)
This is because electrons can be removed from both 4s and 3d orbitals
This is a typical property of transition metals
Explain why copper sulfate solution is blue, but sodium chloride solution is colourless.
Copper is a transition metal with partially filled d orbitals
The Cu²⁺ ion absorbs certain wavelengths of light
Blue light is transmitted, making the solution appear blue
Sodium is a Group 1 metal, not a transition metal
Na⁺ has no partially filled d orbitals
Give one example of a transition metal used as a catalyst and name the industrial process.

The iron provides a surface for the reaction
It speeds up the rate without being used up
Including zinc as a "typical" transition metal
Zinc has full d orbitals, so doesn't show typical properties (coloured ions, variable oxidation states)
Thinking transition metals are more reactive than Group 1
Transition metals are LESS reactive than Group 1
Assuming all transition metal compounds are coloured
Most are, but some (like Zn²⁺ compounds) are white/colourless

Explain why transition metal compounds are often coloured, but Group 1 compounds are usually white. (3 marks)
